baseline_integrity_rules: Use Fate Core escalating-value stress boxes.
Permit at most one stress box per hit.
Do not silently replace skills with Fate Accelerated approaches.
Do not silently replace Core procedures with Condensed or toolkit variants.
Label every independent example and every optional module.
Treat aspects as true even when no fate point is spent.

Fate Condensed.mixing_rule: Choose a baseline and explicitly label imported rules; this database preserves Fate Core stress and other Core defaults.

five_minute_explanation: One participant is the GM, who presents the world, opposition, and consequences.
Each other participant portrays a proactive, capable protagonist.
The GM describes a situation; players describe intentions and methods; the table resolves uncertain meaningful outcomes.
When a roll is needed, roll four Fate dice, add a skill, and compare the total with opposition.
Aspects are important true statements. Invoke them for bonuses or rerolls; accept compels when they create interesting trouble and earn fate points.
Most rules questions reduce to one of four actions: overcome, create an advantage, attack, or defend.
minimum_materials: A character sheet or digital record for each protagonist.
Four Fate dice or four ordinary d6 converted as 1–2 = minus, 3–4 = blank, 5–6 = plus.
Cards or notes for aspects, boosts, consequences, and zones.
A shared premise and an initial problem.
first_session_teaching_order: Explain four Fate dice and the ladder.
Teach overcome and create an advantage.
Demonstrate one paid or free invocation.
Add attack, defense, stress, and consequences only when a conflict occurs.
End with a minor milestone and ask what changed.

first_session_blueprint.length: About two to four hours, adjusted for the group.
first_session_blueprint.setup: One current issue, one important face, two or three locations, and a problem that demands action.
scenes: Opening scene that puts one character aspect under pressure.
Information or social scene with an opportunity to create an advantage.
Challenge or contest that teaches multiple action types.
Climactic conflict or difficult choice where concession is explained.

player_preparation: Know your five aspects or leave clearly marked quick-creation blanks.
Mark your Great and Good skills.
Start with fate points equal to refresh unless scenario carryover applies.
Keep several aspect phrases visible so the table remembers to invoke and compel them.

session_zero_and_table_practice.classification: Recommended table practice; not a single mandatory Fate Core subsystem.
decisions: Agree on genre, tone, premise, and scale.
Choose Fate Core as baseline and identify any Condensed, Accelerated, toolkit, or custom imports.
Agree on the meaning and limits of mental and physical conflict.
Define whether taken out can include death, capture, transformation, public disgrace, or other permanent results.
Discuss content boundaries, pause/check-in tools, accessibility needs, and how to revise a scene.
Choose the skill list, extras, weapon/armor rules, and any setting-specific permissions.
Decide how player-versus-player actions and compels will be negotiated.
Set schedule, attendance, note-taking, and advancement expectations.
accessibility_principles: Do not treat disability, neurodivergence, or mental illness as a generic penalty without the player's request and a specific table agreement.
Let aspects describe access needs, equipment, identity, expertise, and barriers with the same narrative authority as other facts.
Separate player access accommodations from character mechanics.
Offer text, audio, visual, and pacing supports where practical.
Permit breaks and rules reminders without a mechanical cost.

how_to_play_research_guide.one_paragraph_summary: The group describes a shared fictional world and follows proactive, competent protagonists through dramatic problems. When an outcome is uncertain and meaningfully opposed, a player rolls four Fate dice, adds an appropriate skill, and compares the total to active or passive opposition. Aspects make important fictional facts mechanically relevant: fate points invoke helpful aspects, while compels turn aspects into complications that earn fate points. Most uncertain actions are classified as overcome, create an advantage, attack, or defend. Extended situations use challenges, contests, or conflicts.

recommended_group_size.official_default_note: One participant is the GM; the remaining participants each normally portray one protagonist.

player: Describe what the character says, attempts, and feels.
Choose skills and stunts when rules are needed.
Track aspects, stress, consequences, refresh, and fate points.
Help create setting details and support the other protagonists' spotlight.
gamemaster: Portray the world and non-player characters.
Present obstacles, opposition, consequences, and opportunities.
Set passive difficulties or roll active opposition.
Judge whether an aspect invocation, stunt, or declared detail fits the fiction.
Use the protagonists' aspects and the game's issues to build scenarios.
shared_authority: Everyone contributes ideas and asks questions about the setting.
The group establishes what aspects mean in the fiction.
The GM is the final rules arbiter, but Fate expects conversation and consensus rather than adversarial rule enforcement.

required_or_standard: Paper or a digital space for notes.
At least four Fate or Fudge dice, preferably four per participant.
Tokens or counters for fate points.
optional_but_helpful: Index cards or digital cards for aspects, boosts, zones, NPCs, and consequences.
A simple sketch or shared board for conflict zones.
The official Fate Core cheat sheet and worksheets.

core_play_principles.instruction: Describe intent and method before choosing a rule. The fiction determines whether a roll is needed, which skill applies, what opposition exists, and what outcomes make sense.

core_play_principles.principle: Roll only when both uncertainty and meaningful opposition exist
core_play_principles.instruction: Do not roll for routine actions with no interesting failure or cost. Say what happens and continue.
An aspect is not merely a bonus label. It can grant or remove fictional permission, justify opposition, make actions impossible until circumstances change, be invoked, or be compelled.
A failed overcome roll may mean failure, success at a serious cost, or a new mechanical or fictional complication. Avoid dead ends when a cost or twist is more interesting.
Characters are expected to act on problems, possess meaningful competence, and have aspects that create both advantages and trouble.
Create advantages and collect free invocations before a crucial roll instead of relying only on repeated attacks or unmodified skill checks.

game_creation.purpose: Establish the shared premise and create enough setting material to make the first scenario personal and actionable.

steps.name: Choose a premise
instructions: Agree on genre, tone, and the kind of protagonists the group will portray.
State what the protagonists do repeatedly during play.
Confirm that the premise supports proactive, capable characters with dramatic lives.

steps.name: Choose the scale
instructions: Decide whether the story focuses on a neighborhood, city, nation, world, galaxy, or another meaningful scope.
Keep the initial map and lore limited to places the protagonists can affect.
steps.output: A statement of narrative and geographic scale.

steps.name: Define major issues
instructions: Create two setting issues by default.
Use current issues for active problems already affecting the world.
Use impending issues for threats that will become severe if unaddressed.
A common default is one current issue and one impending issue.
steps.output: Two game aspects after character creation.

steps.name: Create faces and places
instructions: Name a few important locations, organizations, and NPCs tied to the issues.
Give each important face or place a concise aspect that explains its story role.
Do not overbuild; add details during play.
steps.output: A small playable network of locations, organizations, and NPCs.

steps.name: Review skills and extras
instructions: Use the default skill list or modify it to emphasize the setting.
Define any supernatural powers, special gear, organizations, or other extras that require rules.
Agree on what ordinary skills can accomplish without a stunt.
steps.output: The campaign's final skill list and any setting-specific extras.

skills.unlisted_default: Mediocre (+0), unless the campaign says an untrained skill is unavailable

final_character_checklist.stress: Two physical and two mental stress boxes by default, modified by Physique and Will.
final_character_checklist.extreme_consequence: One last-resort 8-shift option between major milestones.

steps.name: High concept
steps.instruction: Write an aspect summarizing the character's central identity, role, calling, or defining nature. It should imply capabilities, responsibilities, and likely complications.
tests: Does it quickly tell the table who this character is?
Can it help in several relevant situations?
Can it create obligations, enemies, prejudice, limitations, or difficult choices?

steps.name: Trouble
steps.instruction: Write an aspect representing a recurring personal problem, dangerous relationship, temptation, duty, enemy, weakness, or other source of drama.
tests: Will this reliably complicate the character's life?
Does it invite decisions rather than remove the character's agency?
Can it also occasionally be useful?

steps.name: Name
steps.instruction: Choose the character's name and any title or identity details the group needs.

steps.name: Phase one: first adventure
steps.instruction: Briefly summarize a notable recent adventure starring this character, then create one aspect drawn from it.

steps.name: Phase two: crossing paths
steps.instruction: Add another protagonist to the first adventure, describe that character's role, and create an aspect reflecting the connection or lesson.

steps.name: Phase three: crossing paths again
steps.instruction: Participate in a different protagonist's adventure, describe the role, and create the fifth aspect.

steps.name: Skills
steps.instruction: Assign the default pyramid: one Great (+4), two Good (+3), three Fair (+2), and four Average (+1). Skills not selected normally function at Mediocre (+0).

steps.name: Stunts and refresh
steps.instruction: Choose three free stunts. A fourth or fifth stunt each lowers refresh by one. Refresh may never be lower than 1.

steps.name: Stress and consequences
steps.instruction: Record physical and mental stress boxes and consequence slots. Apply additions from Physique, Will, stunts, or campaign extras.

aspect_quality_guidelines: Make aspects specific enough to inspire scenes.
Phrase them so they can be invoked and compelled.
Prefer an interesting double edge over a purely positive trait.
Leave an aspect blank temporarily rather than choosing an uninspiring phrase.

quick_creation_variant.use_when: The group needs to begin immediately.
minimum_starting_information: refresh of 3 before later stunt adjustments
procedure: Fill in trouble, remaining aspects, skills, and stunts when they become relevant during play.
After the session, complete the sheet and correct refresh for any extra stunts chosen.

when_to_roll: The attempted action has an uncertain result.
There is active opposition from a character or passive opposition from circumstances.
Both success and failure or cost would matter to the story.

roll_steps.instruction: State the character's intent and method.
Identify the action type: overcome, create an advantage, attack, or defend.
Choose the skill justified by the fiction.
Establish active opposition or a passive difficulty.
Roll four Fate dice and add the skill rating.
Compare totals. The difference is measured in shifts.
Before finalizing, invoke relevant aspects or use stunts if desired and permitted.
Apply the outcome for the chosen action, then narrate how the fiction changes.

opposition.active: An opposing character rolls an appropriate skill. Compare the two totals.
opposition.passive: The GM sets a ladder rating representing environment, time pressure, quality, concealment, or other resistance.
opposition.no_opposition: Do not roll unless uncertainty or a meaningful cost still exists.

shifts.definition: The amount by which one total exceeds another.
uses: Determine the value of a successful attack hit.
Measure progress or effect where a subsystem calls for it.

general_outcomes.general_result: The character does not achieve the intent, achieves it at a serious cost, or suffers another meaningful negative result.
The character usually gets a lesser result or succeeds at a minor cost; exact results depend on the action.
The character achieves the intent without added cost.
The character succeeds and receives an additional benefit defined by the action.

difficulty_guidance.Average_1: Use when nothing about the obstacle is especially notable.
difficulty_guidance.near_character_skill: Creates tension without strongly forcing fate-point expenditure.
difficulty_guidance.two_or_more_above_skill: Likely requires preparation, advantages, stunts, or fate points.
difficulty_guidance.two_or_more_below_skill: Lets a competent character demonstrate expertise.
difficulty_guidance.principle: Set difficulty for dramatic importance and established fictional facts, not merely to simulate every physical detail.

aspects_and_fate_points.aspect_definition: A concise phrase describing a significant true fact about a character, object, location, relationship, organization, scene, or the game itself.
aspect_functions: Identify what the story should focus on.
Provide bonuses or rerolls through invocations.

aspect_types.duration: Long-term, though milestones may change it

aspect_types.scope: A scene, zone, object, or character
aspect_types.duration: Until overcome, made irrelevant, or the scene ends
Usually until invoked once or until the opportunity passes

fate_point_refresh.session_rule: At the start of a session within an ongoing scenario, raise the player's fate-point total to refresh if it is lower; keep a higher carried total.
fate_point_refresh.new_scenario_rule: At the start of a new scenario, reset the player's fate-point total to refresh.

spending_fate_points.requirements: Explain why the aspect is relevant.
choose_one_effect: Add +2 to the current roll after seeing the dice.
Give +2 to another character's roll when the aspect can help.
Add +2 to passive opposition, or establish Fair (+2) passive opposition where appropriate.

spending_fate_points.cost: Usually 1 when the stunt says so
spending_fate_points.requirements: Follow the stunt's trigger and limits.
Pay after the compel is proposed and negotiated.
Base the detail on an aspect, keep it plausible and useful, and obtain GM approval.

how_gained: Succeed when creating an advantage: one free invocation.
Succeed with style when creating an advantage: two free invocations.
Inflict a consequence: the attacker gets one free invocation on it.
Receive a boost from an action outcome.
rules: A free invocation grants the same mechanical choices as a paid invocation but costs no fate point.
Free invocations can be passed to allies.
Multiple free invocations may be stacked.
A free invocation may be stacked with one paid invocation on the same aspect for the same roll.
After all free invocations are used, a persistent aspect may still be invoked by spending fate points.

hostile_invocation.definition: Invoking an aspect attached to or effectively controlled by another PC against that character or their interests.
hostile_invocation.payment: The affected player receives the fate point, but it normally becomes available after the scene.
examples: an advantage attached to the target
significant gear controlled by the target

compels.purpose: Turn an aspect into a complication, difficult decision, or unfavorable event that makes the story more dramatic.
procedure: Identify a relevant aspect.
State the proposed complication and why it follows from the aspect.
Negotiate until the table understands the consequence.
The affected player accepts and gains a fate point, or pays a fate point to refuse.

types.pattern: Because the character has this aspect in this situation, it makes sense that the character would choose a troublesome course.
Because this aspect is present in this situation, it makes sense that an unfortunate event would occur.

initiators.GM: May offer a compel without paying a fate point.
initiators.player_on_self: May propose a self-compel without paying a fate point.
initiators.player_on_another_character: Pays one fate point to propose the compel; the target then accepts for a point from the GM's unlimited award pool or pays a point to refuse.

compels.important_limit: Once accepted, the negotiated complication happens. A skill roll cannot erase the complication itself, though characters can respond to the new situation it creates.
compels.retroactive_compel: When an aspect has already produced a clear complication through play, the table may recognize it afterward and award the fate point, subject to GM approval.

earning_fate_points: Receive payment after a hostile invocation of an aspect attached to or controlled by the character.
Concede a conflict: gain one fate point plus one for each consequence taken during that conflict.

GM_fate_points.award_pool: Unlimited for paying accepted compels and concessions.
GM_fate_points.NPC_scene_budget: At the start of a scene, the GM gets one fate point per PC present, usable for any NPC in that scene.
GM_fate_points.reset: Reset the ordinary NPC pool at the beginning of each scene.
carryover_exceptions: A compel that ends one scene or starts the next can add an extra point to the next relevant scene.
Fate points earned by an NPC concession can carry into the next relevant scene.
Hostile invocations against NPC-controlled aspects may provide points for the next scene under the SRD clarification.

overcome.intent: Remove an obstacle, accomplish a task, escape a restriction, or get past opposition.

outcomes.fail: Do not accomplish the intent, or accomplish it only at a serious cost chosen or negotiated to fit the fiction.
outcomes.tie: Accomplish the intent at a minor cost or with a lesser effect.
outcomes.succeed_with_style: Accomplish the intent and gain a boost.

create_an_advantage.intent: Create a new situation aspect, discover an existing aspect, or add free invocations to an aspect already known.
create_an_advantage.required_declaration: Before rolling, state whether the character is creating a new aspect or using/discovering an existing aspect.

new_aspect_outcomes.fail: The aspect is not created, or it is created but a character who benefits to the acting character's detriment receives the free invocation.
new_aspect_outcomes.tie: Create a boost instead of a lasting aspect.
new_aspect_outcomes.succeed: Create the aspect with one free invocation.
new_aspect_outcomes.succeed_with_style: Create the aspect with two free invocations.

existing_aspect_outcomes.fail: Give one free invocation on that aspect to an opposing or otherwise detrimentally positioned character.
existing_aspect_outcomes.tie: Place one free invocation on the aspect.
existing_aspect_outcomes.succeed: Place one free invocation on the aspect.
existing_aspect_outcomes.succeed_with_style: Place two free invocations on the aspect.

create_an_advantage.best_practice: Use this action to set up a later decisive roll, reveal hidden truths, change positioning, or make an opponent vulnerable.

attack.intent: Harm an opponent in a physical or mental conflict, potentially taking them out.
attack.requirement: The acting character must have both the intent and fictional ability to cause harm.

outcomes.fail: Cause no harm. The defender may gain an effect from succeeding with style on the defense.
outcomes.tie: Cause no harm and gain a boost.
outcomes.succeed: Inflict a hit equal to the shifts of success.
outcomes.succeed_with_style: Inflict the full hit, or reduce the hit by one shift to gain a boost.

defend.intent: Prevent an attack from causing harm or stop another character from creating an advantage against the defender.
defend.timing: A reaction made when targeted; it does not consume the defender's later action.

outcomes.fail: Suffer the attack hit or the advantage outcome.
outcomes.tie: Avoid the main effect but grant the opponent a boost.
outcomes.succeed_with_style: Avoid the effect and gain a boost.

defend.overcome_clarification: There is no special defend action against overcome. A character who is directly in the way can still provide active opposition, but does not gain defend's special outcome benefits.

combining_skills.use_when: Several characters apply the same skill toward one action.
procedure: Choose the participant with the highest relevant skill as lead.
Each helper with at least Average (+1) in that same skill adds +1.
Only the lead character rolls.
combining_skills.failure: Costs or complications may affect all participants because all shared the attempt.

stacking_advantages.use_when: Characters contribute different setup actions toward a single important roll.
procedure: Each helper creates an appropriate advantage.
Pass free invocations to the character making the decisive roll.
The acting character stacks relevant free and paid invocations as allowed.

challenge.use_when: A complicated objective contains several distinct tasks, but the characters are not directly competing for the same goal and are not trying to harm each other.
procedure: List the major tasks that must be completed.
Assign an appropriate skill and opposition to each task.
Resolve each as an overcome action, normally using different skills or approaches.
Interpret all results together to determine overall success, costs, and complications.
challenge.create_advantage_option: Characters may create advantages before or during the challenge when the fiction permits.
challenge.boundary: If direct attacks become central, move to a conflict.

contest.use_when: Two or more sides pursue mutually exclusive goals without directly trying to harm one another.
procedure: Each exchange, every side makes an appropriate contest roll.
The highest total gains one victory.
If the highest side succeeds with style and no other side does, it gains two victories.
If the highest totals tie, nobody gains a victory; introduce an unexpected twist or new situation aspect.
The first side to three victories wins.
contest.team_sides: Multiple characters on one side use teamwork.
contest.create_advantage_option: A character may roll to create an advantage before the side's contest roll; failing that setup roll forfeits that character's contribution to the contest roll for the exchange.
contest.boundary: If a participant attacks and the intent and ability to harm are real, transition to a conflict.

conflict.use_when: Characters have both the intent and ability to harm one another physically or mentally.
setup: Write three to five useful situation aspects where appropriate.
Divide the space into a few meaningful zones.
exchange_loop: On a character's turn, move if desired and allowed.
Other characters defend or provide active opposition when targeted.
After every participant has acted, begin a new exchange.
conflict.ending_condition: The conflict ends when all members of one side have conceded, been taken out, or no longer have the intent or ability to cause harm.

zones.definition: A loose area whose occupants can normally interact directly without overcoming distance.
design_guidelines: Use only as many zones as are tactically or narratively meaningful.
Boundaries should reflect barriers, distance, cover, height, doors, crowds, or other notable changes.
Fate zones are abstract and do not require exact measurements.
zones.situation_aspects: Write a few evocative environmental facts such as Poor Lighting, Slick Floor, Heavy Cover, or Roaring Crowd.

turn_order.sequence: Highest rating acts first, then descending.
turn_order.simple_GM_option: Use the most advantageous NPC's placement and let the GM's NPCs act together.

movement.free_movement: Move one zone in addition to the action when nothing meaningfully obstructs movement.
overcome_required_when: a situation aspect makes movement difficult
movement.action_cost: The overcome roll normally uses the character's action for that exchange.

turn_options: Overcome an obstacle or restrictive aspect.
Create an advantage for oneself or an ally.
Concede before a roll that would affect the conceding character.
advantages_in_conflict: Attack an opponent's position instead of stress by creating an aspect such as Disarmed or Pinned.
Use the environment to create aspects and free invocations.
Pass setup invocations to a teammate for a strong finishing action.
An aspect may also create an obstacle or deny permission even after its free invocations are spent.

harm_stress_consequences.hit_value: A successful attack inflicts a hit equal to the attacker's shifts over the defense.
harm_stress_consequences.absorption_goal: Use stress, consequences, or both to absorb every shift of the hit. If any shifts remain unabsorbed, the character is taken out.

stress.meaning: Short-term exertion, lost momentum, near misses, superficial harm, or momentary emotional strain.
stress.core_specific_rule: Only one stress box may be checked for each hit.
how_to_use: Check an unused box whose value is equal to the remaining hit.
If that exact box is unavailable, check one unused box with a higher value.
Unused capacity in a higher box is lost; it does not carry to another hit.
stress.recovery: Clear stress after the conflict when the character has a moment to rest or regain composure.

consequences.meaning: Lasting physical, mental, social, or other harm expressed as an aspect.
use_rules: Each consequence reduces a hit by its shift value.
More than one consequence may be taken on one hit if slots are available.
Any remaining shifts must be absorbed by one stress box.
The attacker receives one free invocation on each consequence inflicted.
Physical and mental harm share the standard consequence slots.

recovery_action.fictional_requirement: Appropriate treatment, counseling, rest, repair, reputation work, or another method fitting the harm.
recovery_action.self_treatment_modifier: Increase difficulty by two ladder steps when treating oneself.
recovery_action.success_effect: Rename or mark the consequence to show recovery has begun, then wait the required period before clearing the slot.

physique_and_will_adjustments.physical: Physique modifies physical stress and may add a physical-only mild consequence.
physique_and_will_adjustments.mental: Will modifies mental stress and may add a mental-only mild consequence.

extreme_consequence.cost: Replace one character aspect other than the high concept with the extreme consequence.
extreme_consequence.recovery: It cannot be cleared through a normal recovery action. At a major milestone, rename it to reflect lasting change and regain the ability to take another extreme consequence.
extreme_consequence.design_intent: A last-resort option that permanently changes the character rather than functioning as ordinary healing.

taken_out.trigger: The character cannot or chooses not to absorb every shift of a hit.
taken_out.effect: The character is removed from the conflict, and the victor gains strong authority to narrate the defeat within the conflict's established scope.
taken_out.scope_limit: The result must follow from the stakes and methods established in the conflict.
taken_out.death_and_permanent_harm: Discuss these stakes before play or before the relevant conflict; Fate Core explicitly recommends group agreement about how severe taken-out results may be.

concession.timing: Declare at any time before dice are rolled for the action that would affect the conceding character.
effect: The opposing side gets what it primarily wanted or the conceding character is removed as an obstacle.
The conceding player retains input into the exact terms and avoids the least acceptable taken-out result.
The terms must be a meaningful loss, not a disguised victory.
concession.fate_point_award: One fate point for conceding, plus one for each consequence the character took during that conflict.
concession.availability: Awarded points are usable after the conflict.

end_of_conflict_cleanup: Distribute fate points earned from concessions and hostile invocations.
Keep consequences until recovery is complete.
Update situation and story aspects to reflect the outcome.

alternative_columns.rule: Maintain supporting skills beneath higher ratings, as used during advancement.

default_skills.name: Athletics
default_skills.summary: Movement, balance, acrobatics, sprinting, and physically avoiding danger.

default_skills.name: Burglary
default_skills.summary: Locks, security systems, casing locations, theft, and criminal intrusion.

default_skills.name: Contacts
default_skills.summary: Social networks, informants, reputation within communities, and finding people or information through connections.
common_uses: resist attacks on reputation when appropriate

default_skills.name: Crafts
default_skills.summary: Building, repairing, modifying, sabotaging, and understanding machines or constructed objects.

default_skills.name: Deceive
default_skills.summary: Lying, disguise, misdirection, feints, and concealing motives.
common_uses: resist attempts to read or expose a deception

default_skills.name: Drive
default_skills.summary: Operating vehicles and performing difficult maneuvers or chases.

default_skills.name: Empathy
default_skills.summary: Reading emotions and motives, recognizing changes in behavior, and providing emotional support.

default_skills.name: Fight
default_skills.summary: Close-quarters combat with fists, melee weapons, and similar methods.
common_uses: break through by force in a fight

default_skills.name: Investigate
default_skills.summary: Careful, deliberate examination, evidence gathering, research, and reconstruction of events.

default_skills.name: Lore
default_skills.summary: Education, scholarship, specialist knowledge, and recalling or researching facts.

default_skills.name: Notice
default_skills.summary: Immediate awareness, alertness, quick perception, and spotting things without prolonged study.

default_skills.name: Physique
default_skills.summary: Strength, endurance, toughness, and feats of raw physical power.

default_skills.name: Provoke
default_skills.summary: Intimidation, threats, anger, fear, and deliberately pushing emotional buttons.
common_uses: make mental attacks when harm is possible

default_skills.name: Rapport
default_skills.summary: Honest persuasion, charm, trust-building, diplomacy, and positive social connection.
common_uses: defend against social pressure when appropriate

default_skills.name: Resources
default_skills.summary: Wealth, credit, purchasing power, and access to material assets.

default_skills.name: Shoot

stunts.definition: A special exception or focused benefit that changes how a skill or another rule works for one character.

common_design_patterns.template: Gain +2 to a named skill when using a named action under a narrow, recurring circumstance.
Use one named skill instead of another for one action in a clearly limited situation.
Gain a focused capability not normally available, with explicit limits or a fate-point cost if especially strong.

quality_tests: Does it have a clear trigger?
Is its scope narrow enough to make other choices matter?
Does it reinforce the character concept?
Does it specify action, skill, circumstance, duration, and cost where needed?
stunts.refresh_cost: The fourth and fifth starting stunts each reduce refresh by one.

fate_point_decision_guide.situation: A roll is crucial and a relevant aspect clearly helps.
The dice result is -3 or -4 and success matters.
fate_point_decision_guide.recommended_tool: A reroll is often more valuable than +2.

fate_point_decision_guide.situation: The roll is not yet strong enough for a decisive effect.
fate_point_decision_guide.recommended_tool: Create advantages first and stack free invocations.
Accept or propose a compel to generate drama and gain a fate point.

fate_point_decision_guide.situation: A useful setting detail would follow from a character aspect.
fate_point_decision_guide.recommended_tool: Spend a fate point to declare the detail, subject to table approval.

fate_point_decision_guide.situation: A conflict is turning dangerous and being taken out would remove narrative control.
fate_point_decision_guide.recommended_tool: Concede before the next relevant roll.

advancement.principle: Fate advancement often changes a character to reflect the story before it simply raises numbers.
advancement.skill_column_requirement: When increasing a skill, maintain a valid column: every skill above Average (+1) must be supported by at least one more skill at the rating immediately below it.

milestones.typical_timing: End of a session or resolution of a smaller story beat.
choose_one: Switch the ratings of any two skills.
Replace one Average (+1) skill with a skill not currently rated.
Buy a new stunt if sufficient refresh remains and refresh will not fall below 1.
Rename one character aspect other than the high concept.
milestones.additional_recovery_option: Rename a moderate consequence to begin recovery if appropriate.

milestones.typical_timing: End of a scenario, major plot event, or roughly every two or three sessions.
benefits: Receive all benefits of a minor milestone.
Gain one skill point to buy a new Average (+1) skill or raise a skill by one step while maintaining valid columns.
milestones.additional_recovery_option: Rename a severe consequence to begin recovery if appropriate.

milestones.typical_timing: End of an arc or a campaign-changing event.
benefits: Receive all benefits of significant and minor milestones.
Gain one refresh, which may be kept or spent on a stunt.
Raise a skill beyond the current campaign cap when the column supports it, thereby raising the cap.
Rename the high concept if desired.
Rename an extreme consequence to represent permanent change and regain the ability to take another later.
milestones.world_effect: Review and change game issues, faces, places, and opposition to reflect the protagonists' impact.

scene_framing: Start scenes close to a meaningful choice, obstacle, revelation, or interaction.
State where the characters are, what is happening now, and what makes the scene matter.
Ask players for details tied to their characters and aspects.
End a scene when its question is answered, its purpose is exhausted, or a strong transition is available.
using_aspects_for_prep: Select character aspects that have not recently received spotlight.
Connect game issues to character troubles, relationships, and goals.
Build scenario problems that cannot be solved by inaction.
Give important NPCs and places aspects that invite interaction.
setting_opposition: Use passive opposition for environment, quality, time pressure, or an NPC who is not actively resisting.
Use active opposition when a character can meaningfully respond.
Let high skills look impressive when the scene is not meant to be a major challenge.
Use high difficulties when established fiction or dramatic stakes justify characters spending resources or preparing advantages.
Do not hide an unavoidable outcome behind a meaningless roll.
costs_on_failure: A new enemy, hazard, or complication.
Success that creates a serious new problem.

NPC_scaling.nameless_NPCs: Give only the few skill ratings, aspects, stress, or group rules needed for the scene. Very minor NPCs may be overcome as an obstacle or taken out by a one-shift hit.
NPC_scaling.supporting_NPCs: Give a small set of relevant skills, a few aspects or stunts, and enough stress or consequences for their role.
NPC_scaling.main_NPCs: Build close to a PC when the character is a recurring central figure, but include only mechanics that will actually enter play.
NPC_scaling.principle: Stat the opposition for its dramatic purpose, not as a complete simulation.

compel_practice: Offer compels that create a real complication or difficult choice.
Tie them to an explicit aspect.
Do not use a compel merely to cancel a player's successful action.
Use retroactive compels when a player has already leaned into an aspect's trouble.

safety_and_stakes.status: Recommended table practice rather than a unique Fate Core subsystem.
recommendations: Agree on tone, content boundaries, and the severity of physical and mental conflict.
Establish whether taken out can include death, capture, transformation, public disgrace, or other permanent outcomes.
Use a pause, check-in, or safety tool when a scene becomes uncomfortable.
Treat mental conflict consequences as fictional drama, not clinical diagnosis.

worked_examples.title: Basic overcome roll
worked_examples.setup: A character with Burglary Good (+3) tries to bypass a Great (+4) lock before guards arrive.
worked_examples.resolution: The lock opens, but the GM applies a minor cost, such as leaving evidence or consuming extra time.

worked_examples.title: Create an advantage and pass the setup
worked_examples.setup: One character uses Provoke to make a guard Recklessly Angry so an ally can slip past.
worked_examples.mechanical_effect: Create the situation aspect Recklessly Angry with one free invocation.
worked_examples.teamwork: Pass the free invocation to the ally, who may invoke it for +2 or a reroll on a relevant Stealth action.

worked_examples.title: Attack, consequence, and stress
worked_examples.setup: An attacker wins a Fight attack by 5 shifts.
one_valid_absorption: Take a moderate consequence to absorb 4 shifts.
Check the 1-point physical stress box to absorb the remaining shift.
worked_examples.result: The target stays in the conflict. The consequence is an aspect, and the attacker receives one free invocation on it.

worked_examples.title: Success with style on an attack
worked_examples.setup: An attack beats defense by 4 shifts.
options: Inflict a 3-shift hit and gain a boost.

worked_examples.title: Compel
worked_examples.situation: The safe route closes while a trapped ally calls for help.
worked_examples.offer: Because the character never leaves anyone behind, it makes sense that they turn back and lose the safe escape. Accept the complication for one fate point or pay one fate point to refuse.
worked_examples.important_note: If accepted, the character turns back; subsequent rolls address the rescue and its new dangers rather than negating the agreed complication.

worked_examples.title: Concession
worked_examples.setup: A character has taken one mild and one moderate consequence and sees that the next attack may take them out.
worked_examples.timing: Before the attacker's dice are rolled, the player concedes.
worked_examples.negotiated_loss: The enemy gets the artifact, but the character escapes alive and is not captured.
worked_examples.calculation: 1 for conceding + 1 for each of the two consequences taken in this conflict

common_rules_confusions.confusion: Aspects only matter when fate points are spent.
common_rules_confusions.correction: Aspects are always true and may grant permission, deny permission, or justify opposition even without an invocation.

common_rules_confusions.confusion: A tie always means nothing happens.
common_rules_confusions.correction: Tie results depend on the action; they often produce a cost, boost, or free invocation.

common_rules_confusions.confusion: Every failed roll blocks the story.
common_rules_confusions.correction: An overcome failure may instead succeed at a serious cost or introduce a complication.

common_rules_confusions.confusion: Fate Core stress boxes are one-point boxes.
common_rules_confusions.correction: Core uses escalating box values and allows only one stress box per hit. One-point stress boxes are a common later variant, including Fate Condensed's default.
Stress is temporary pressure or near-harm. Consequences carry lasting injuries or setbacks.

common_rules_confusions.confusion: Defending uses up the character's turn.
common_rules_confusions.correction: Defense is a reaction and does not replace the character's own action.

common_rules_confusions.confusion: A compel is a forced action with no discussion.
common_rules_confusions.correction: A compel is proposed and negotiated; the affected player accepts for a fate point or pays to refuse.

glossary.definition: One of the four mechanical intents: overcome, create an advantage, attack, or defend.
Resistance represented by another character's roll.
A significant true phrase that can influence fiction and mechanics.
A short-lived, one-use advantage functioning like a free invocation.
A negotiated complication arising from an aspect that awards a fate point when accepted.
Leaving a conflict before a relevant roll in exchange for a meaningful loss, retained input on the outcome, and fate points.
A lasting harm aspect used to absorb hit shifts.
One conflict round in which each participant gets a turn.
A token spent to invoke aspects, refuse compels, declare details, or activate certain stunts.
An aspect invocation that does not cost a fate point.
An invocation of another character's attached or controlled aspect against that character or their interests.
Use an aspect for +2, a reroll, aid, or increased passive opposition.
The adjective-and-number scale used for skills, difficulties, and results.
A story breakpoint that permits character or world change and advancement.
A fixed difficulty representing environmental or situational resistance.
The baseline fate-point total a character receives at refresh time.
One point of difference between two compared totals.
Short-term capacity used to absorb a hit without taking lasting consequences.
A focused special rule that improves or changes a character's use of skills or other mechanics.
Beat opposition by three or more shifts and gain the action's extra benefit.
Removal from a conflict when a hit cannot be fully absorbed, giving the victor strong authority over the defeat.
An abstract area used to track meaningful position and movement in a conflict.

overcome.intent: Remove an obstacle, accomplish a task, escape a restriction, or get past opposition.

outcomes.fail: Do not accomplish the intent, or accomplish it only at a serious cost chosen or negotiated to fit the fiction.
outcomes.tie: Accomplish the intent at a minor cost or with a lesser effect.
outcomes.succeed_with_style: Accomplish the intent and gain a boost.

create_an_advantage.intent: Create a new situation aspect, discover an existing aspect, or add free invocations to an aspect already known.
create_an_advantage.required_declaration: Before rolling, state whether the character is creating a new aspect or using/discovering an existing aspect.

new_aspect_outcomes.fail: The aspect is not created, or it is created but a character who benefits to the acting character's detriment receives the free invocation.
new_aspect_outcomes.tie: Create a boost instead of a lasting aspect.
new_aspect_outcomes.succeed: Create the aspect with one free invocation.
new_aspect_outcomes.succeed_with_style: Create the aspect with two free invocations.

existing_aspect_outcomes.fail: Give one free invocation on that aspect to an opposing or otherwise detrimentally positioned character.
existing_aspect_outcomes.tie: Place one free invocation on the aspect.
existing_aspect_outcomes.succeed: Place one free invocation on the aspect.
existing_aspect_outcomes.succeed_with_style: Place two free invocations on the aspect.

create_an_advantage.best_practice: Use this action to set up a later decisive roll, reveal hidden truths, change positioning, or make an opponent vulnerable.

attack.intent: Harm an opponent in a physical or mental conflict, potentially taking them out.
attack.requirement: The acting character must have both the intent and fictional ability to cause harm.

outcomes.fail: Cause no harm. The defender may gain an effect from succeeding with style on the defense.
outcomes.tie: Cause no harm and gain a boost.
outcomes.succeed: Inflict a hit equal to the shifts of success.
outcomes.succeed_with_style: Inflict the full hit, or reduce the hit by one shift to gain a boost.

defend.intent: Prevent an attack from causing harm or stop another character from creating an advantage against the defender.
defend.timing: A reaction made when targeted; it does not consume the defender's later action.

outcomes.fail: Suffer the attack hit or the advantage outcome.
outcomes.tie: Avoid the main effect but grant the opponent a boost.
outcomes.succeed_with_style: Avoid the effect and gain a boost.

defend.overcome_clarification: There is no special defend action against overcome. A character who is directly in the way can still provide active opposition, but does not gain defend's special outcome benefits.

fate_core_stress_correction.rule: Fate Core uses escalating box values. Only one stress box may absorb a hit.
fate_core_stress_correction.physical_track_formula: Base [1,2]; Physique +1 or +2 adds [3]; Physique +3 or +4 adds [3,4]; Physique +5 or more also adds a physical-only mild consequence.
fate_core_stress_correction.mental_track_formula: Base [1,2]; Will +1 or +2 adds [3]; Will +3 or +4 adds [3,4]; Will +5 or more also adds a mental-only mild consequence.
fate_core_stress_correction.do_not_silently_mix: Fate Condensed's default one-point boxes are not used in Core calculations.

invoke_comparison.plus_two: Deterministically increases the current margin by two shifts.
invoke_comparison.reroll: Discard all four dice and roll a fresh independent 4dF result; the skill and other bonuses remain.
decision_guidance: Use +2 when two shifts are enough to reach the desired outcome.
A reroll is attractive when the dice total is very low, especially -3 or -4.
The value of success with style, costs, and remaining fate points can outweigh pure probability.
invoke_comparison.reroll_distribution: Identical to the base 4dF distribution because the new roll is independent.

probability_warnings: Fate is not balanced around repeated unmodified rolls; aspects, free invocations, teamwork, and preparation materially change odds.
A tie has action-specific effects and should not be grouped automatically with either failure or full success.
Passive difficulty and active opposition use the same margin categories after totals are compared.

challenge.use_when: The objective contains several distinct tasks whose combined results determine success.
challenge.recommended_tasks: Three to five for a substantial scene.
assembly_rules: Each task should change the fiction even when failed.
Avoid requiring the same skill for every task unless different methods and stakes make the rolls distinct.
Allow created advantages before or during the challenge.
Interpret the results together rather than counting only raw successes.

contest.use_when: Sides seek mutually exclusive goals and are not primarily trying to harm one another.
assembly_rules: Each exchange, compare the sides' rolls.
Highest side gains one victory; a sole success with style gains two.
A tie at the top grants no victory and introduces a twist.
Use teamwork for multiple characters on one side.
Move to conflict if participants gain both intent and ability to cause harm.

conflict.use_when: Participants intend and are able to cause physical or mental harm.
assembly_rules: Agree on the scope of possible taken-out results.
Use zones and scene aspects that create meaningful choices.
Every participant acts once per exchange.
Defense is reactive and does not consume the defender's later action.
End when one side is taken out, concedes, or no longer has intent or ability to cause harm.

rescue_under_pressure.premise: Someone important is trapped while a second danger grows worse.
rescue_under_pressure.initial_question: Who is trapped, why can ordinary authorities not reach them, and what will happen if the group is late?
scene_beats: Cross or bypass the main obstacle.
Reach the victim while opposition closes in.
Resolve the extraction and its cost.
twists: The victim refuses to leave without another person or object.
The apparent captor is protecting the victim from a larger threat.
The safest route strengthens the enemy's position.
success_costs: The protagonists owe a major favor.
The rescue exposes a secret.
A useful location is destroyed.

investigation_with_clock.premise: A hidden cause must be identified before a deadline makes the damage irreversible.
investigation_with_clock.initial_question: What happened, what misleading explanation is accepted, and what deadline prevents endless research?
scene_beats: Confront the person or system benefiting from confusion.
twists: The evidence is genuine but points to the wrong motive.
A witness is truthful and still mistaken.
The culprit is trying to prevent a worse event.
success_costs: The truth destabilizes an institution.
A source is endangered.
The protagonists must choose what not to reveal.

negotiation_at_breaking_point.premise: Two or more factions need an agreement, but public pressure and old harm make compromise dangerous.
negotiation_at_breaking_point.initial_question: What does each side need, what do they publicly demand, and who benefits if talks fail?
scene_beats: Win access to a resistant delegate.
Create leverage without humiliating a side.
Draft a settlement with a real sacrifice.
twists: A delegate lacks authority to accept the best deal.
The saboteur belongs to both sides.
Peace requires admitting a shared crime.
success_costs: The agreement empowers an unpleasant actor.
The protagonists become guarantors.
One ally sees compromise as betrayal.

heist.premise: The group must obtain a protected target through planning, infiltration, and adaptation.
heist.initial_question: What is the target, why can it not simply be bought or requested, and what makes the location uniquely secure?
scene_beats: Acquire access, equipment, or an insider.
twists: The target is a person with their own agenda.
Another crew acts at the same time.
The target was moved because someone predicted the plan.
success_costs: Evidence points toward an ally.
The stolen object creates a new obligation.
The clean escape requires leaving something valuable behind.

hold_the_line.premise: The protagonists must delay or redirect a stronger force until a separate objective is completed.
hold_the_line.initial_question: What must be protected, how long is needed, and why is retreat not yet possible?
scene_beats: Respond to a breach or betrayal.
Complete the objective or negotiate withdrawal.
twists: The enemy offers a sincere ceasefire for an unacceptable price.
The protected objective changes location.
The attackers are fleeing something worse.
success_costs: The position is lost after the objective succeeds.
A defender takes a lasting consequence.
The victory reveals the group's capabilities.

chase_for_control.premise: Opposing sides race for a person, object, location, or transmission before direct confrontation becomes inevitable.
chase_for_control.initial_question: What is being pursued, what counts as securing it, and what terrain makes the chase interesting?
scene_beats: Establish starting positions and route aspects.
Gain or lose the first victory.
Determine who reaches control first and whether violence follows.
twists: The objective moves independently.
The fastest route crosses a moral boundary.
A third faction joins after two victories.
success_costs: The route causes collateral damage.
The objective distrusts the winner.
The losing side learns where the group is going next.

containment_failure.premise: A dangerous system, creature, secret, or supernatural effect is escaping control.
containment_failure.initial_question: What was containment designed to hold, why is it failing now, and who concealed the warning signs?
scene_beats: Choose repair, relocation, negotiation, or destruction.
twists: Containment itself is causing the threat's hostility.
The failure was deliberate but intended as a rescue.
Repair requires releasing a smaller danger.
success_costs: The facility cannot be saved.
A character becomes part of the new seal.
The truth creates political consequences.

public_reckoning.premise: An accusation, trial, election, broadcast, or ceremony will decide public legitimacy.
public_reckoning.initial_question: What judgment is being made, who controls the forum, and what evidence or performance can change the result?
scene_beats: Survive a revelation about the protagonists.
Make the final appeal or decisive exposure.
twists: The audience wants a comforting lie.
The best evidence implicates an ally.
Winning legally would lose the community.
success_costs: The protagonists become public figures.
A private relationship is sacrificed.
The institution changes but does not disappear.
